artists.biography:
Explosions in the Sky is an American post-rock band from Texas. The band has garnered popularity beyond the post-rock scene for their elaborately developed guitar work, narratively styled instrumentals, what they refer to as "cathartic mini-symphonies," and their enthusiastic and emotional live shows.They primarily play with three electric guitars and a drum kit, although band member Michael James will at times exchange his electric guitar for a bass guitar. Recently the band has added a fifth member to their live performances.The band's music is purely instrumental.

Originally called Breaker Morant, Explosions in the Sky was formed in Austin, Texas in 1999. Drummer Chris Hrasky is from Rockford, Illinois, and the rest of the band hails from Midland, Texas. The new name of "Explosions in the Sky" came from a comment Hrasky made in reference to the noise or sightof fireworks when they left KVRX on the night they played their first set and recorded their first track, "Remember Me as a Time of Day", that would be released on a compilation.Their 2000 debut album, How Strange, Innocence, was locally distributed in the form of CD-Rs. Rehearsal footage is featured on the feature film Cicadas, which won an Austin Film Festival award.

perplexity.description:
All of a Sudden I Miss Everyone is the fifth studio album by American post-rock band Explosions in the Sky, released in 2007 on Temporary Residence Limited. The album is a hallmark of the band’s signature instrumental style, blending expansive guitar textures, dynamic crescendos, and emotive melodies. It features six tracks, each unfolding with a cinematic quality that balances melancholy and hope, anchored by the band’s meticulous interplay and atmospheric production. The album’s sound is both intricate and accessible, showcasing the group’s evolution toward more nuanced arrangements and a broader sonic palette.

Within Explosions in the Sky’s discography, All of a Sudden I Miss Everyone stands as a pivotal release, marking a refinement of their post-rock approach and solidifying their reputation as leaders in the genre. The album debuted at number 76 on the Billboard 200, selling 11,000 copies in its first week, and received widespread critical acclaim for its emotional depth and compositional mastery. Its influence extended beyond the rock world, with the album’s artwork even becoming iconic in music culture. The release also included a bonus disc of remixes by notable electronic artists, further bridging the gap between rock and electronic music.
